question: Why is it so important to keep hospital bed sheets completely free of wrinkles?

options.A: To prevent pressure ulcers on the skin
options.B: To make linen last longer in the hospital
options.C: To save time during morning nursing duties
options.D: To make the ward look neat and tidy

explanation: You're doing great! Wrinkles in bed sheets create constant friction and pressure against delicate skin, which can quickly lead to painful pressure sores. Keeping sheets smooth keeps our patients safe and comfortable. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: When stripping a dirty hospital bed, why should you avoid shaking the linen in the air?

options.A: It creates too much noise in the quiet ward
options.B: It makes the laundry department reject the bundle
options.C: It causes the fabric to tear and wear out quickly
options.D: It spreads dust and microorganisms into the environment

explanation: Good instinct! Shaking sheets sends dust, skin flakes, and germs flying into the air where they can float around and land on other clean surfaces. Always roll linen gently away from you instead! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h1)

question: When setting up your linen trolley for bed making, in what order should you stack your items?

options.A: Reverse order of use with the first item at the top
options.B: Reverse order of use with the first item at the bottom
options.C: Chronological order matching the patient's daily routine
options.D: Random order depending on what fits best on the tray

explanation: Think of it like building a puzzle backwards! Putting the very first item you'll need right at the top means you can grab it easily without messing up your neat stack of clean supplies. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main job of the waterproof draw sheet on a hospital bed?

options.A: To decorate the ward with matching institutional colors
options.B: To protect the lower mattress from bodily fluids
options.C: To keep the patient warm during cold harmattan nights
options.D: To prevent the top blanket from slipping off the bed

explanation: Spot on! Mattresses are expensive and hard to clean, so the waterproof draw sheet acts as a trusty shield against accidental spills, sweat, or other body fluids. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is another common name for an admission bed setup in the ward?
explanation: You've got this! We call it 'unoccupied' because no patient is in it yet, and 'open' because the top covers are neatly folded back, ready to welcome a new arrival. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why do we fanfold the top bedclothes to the side when preparing an admission bed?

options.A: To give the housekeeping staff space to mop the floor
options.B: To let the incoming patient get in quickly without effort
options.C: To keep the pillows warm before the doctor examines them
options.D: To allow maximum airflow underneath the foam mattress

explanation: Exactly! When a tired or weak patient is being transferred from a stretcher, fanfolding the sheets clears the path so they can slide right into bed without a struggle. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: What item is usually kept ready on an operation bed to help keep a post-surgery patient warm?
explanation: Well done! Anesthesia can cause a patient's body temperature to drop, so having warm water bottles ready is a classic, caring way to help them stay cozy and safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient is about to return from the theatre after surgery. How should you arrange the top bedclothes?

options.A: Folded or rolled to the side to ease transfer from the trolley
options.B: Removed entirely from the room until the patient regains consciousness
options.C: Drawn up completely to the headboard to preserve body heat
options.D: Tucked tightly at the foot like a standard closed bed

explanation: You're learning fast! Rolling the covers to one side makes it super easy for the nursing team to slide the patient straight from the stretcher without having to lift them over blankets. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why must patients dealing with severe heart failure avoid lying completely flat in bed?

options.A: It slows down digestion and causes severe abdominal cramps
options.B: It increases venous return and worsens fluid in the lungs
options.C: It makes it impossible for the nurse to check blood pressure
options.D: It puts too much pressure on the lower lumbar vertebrae

explanation: Great clinical thinking! When a heart failure patient lies flat, gravity rushes more blood back to the heart all at once. Since the heart is struggling, this causes fluid to back up into the lungs, making it hard to breathe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the clinical reason for placing an over-bed table across a cardiac patient's lap?

options.A: To hold breakfast trays securely during morning ward rounds
options.B: To let the patient lean forward and use accessory breathing muscles
options.C: To prevent the patient from sliding down toward the footboard
options.D: To support heavy cardiac monitor wires and infusion pumps

explanation: Brilliant! Leaning forward onto a bedside table opens up the chest cavity, giving the patient's tired breathing muscles extra leverage to pull air into their lungs much more easily. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the most important safety action a nurse must take right after finishing an occupied bed?

options.A: Strip the extra pillows from the rack
options.B: Wipe down the wheels with antiseptic
options.C: Lock the patient in the room for safety
options.D: Return the bed to its lowest position

explanation: Safety first! Always lower the bed back down before you walk away. A high bed is a major fall hazard if an unsteady patient tries to climb out on their own. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe body mechanic (ergonomic practice) when making a bed?

options.A: Keeping a wide base of support with feet apart for balance
options.B: Adjusting the hospital bed frame to a comfortable waist level
options.C: Bending fully at the waist with straight knees while tucking sheets
options.D: Moving close to the mattress edge to avoid excessive reaching

explanation: Spot on! Bending at the waist with straight knees puts all the strain on your lower back. Always bend your knees and use your legs to protect your spine while working! [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h6)
